Implicit Ads · representations · November 10, 2026

One vector per celebrity and brand, built from five public sources

110 entities · Wikipedia text and reader clicks · news full text · Google related searches · local LLM free association · exploratory

Each entity gets two objects built from the same five sources. A vector places it in a semantic space: what kind of thing it is. An association profile says what it is made of: of everything written, read, searched or recalled about Tate, what share involves Adidas. The first is symmetric. The second is directional, and that is what Ads as Cues needs.

Bottom line

  1. Most ambassador links run forward. Of 73 ambassador pairs, 40 are forward (the brand is a bigger part of the celebrity than the reverse), 12 backward, and 21 flat, mostly because neither side shows up in the other at all, as with Tate × Adidas.
  2. The bigger public memory absorbs the link. Direction tracks relative size: the more Wikipedia views the celebrity has relative to the brand, the more the link runs backward (r = -0.55, permutation p = 0.0000, n = 53). Sweeney × Novig (×14 backward), Federer × On, Elordi × Bottega Veneta and Jung Kook × Calvin Klein are the backward cases; athletes and actresses at Nike and Dior are the forward ones.
  3. Similarity and association come apart (correlation 0.14 across celebrity–brand combinations). Ambassador pairs are not unusually similar; they stand out on association.
  4. Sources can disagree, and that is informative. LeBron × Nike is forward in the LLM (LeBron brings up Nike in 57% of samples) but backward in news, Wikipedia text and clicks, where LeBron is 9% of Nike's coverage. What a model "knows" about a person and what the public reads about a brand differ.

1. Why two objects

A cosine between two vectors is the same in both directions, so it cannot say that Tate calls up Adidas more than Adidas calls up Tate. It measures resemblance: Tate is close to other pop singers, Adidas to Nike and Puma. Association is a different quantity: P(B | A), the share of A's public memory in which B appears. That is what the memory literature calls forward associative strength, and it is what enters the numerator of the Ads as Cues retrieval rule.

sourceA's unitsA → B is the share of A's units that…
Wikipedia textsentences of A's articlename B
NewsCommon Crawl News articles about A (title or description)name B anywhere in the text
Wikipedia clicksclicks leaving A's page, Jul–Oct 2026go to B's page
Google searchestop related queries for A (US, Nov 2025–Oct 2026)name B (weighted by Google's index)
LLM30 free-association lists from Qwen3-8Bname B

The vector is the weighted mean embedding (bge-base) of the same units, computed per source, normalized and averaged across sources. A masked version replaces every frame name with [NAME], so similarity cannot come from the names themselves.

Strength is the mean, across sources, of where the share ranks among all non-zero associations observed in that source (0 = absent, 1 = the strongest). Asymmetry is the geometric mean, across sources with both directions, of the ratio of the two shares (each padded by a tenth of the source's median non-zero share).

5. Coverage and caveats

sourceentities with enough datamedian units
Wikipedia article (share of sentences naming the other)81 / 110147
Common Crawl News (share of articles about the entity whose text names the other)35 / 11025
Wikipedia readers (share of outgoing clicks to the other's page)95 / 110137,890
Google related searches, US (share of related-query weight naming the other)65 / 11025
Qwen3-8B free association (share of samples naming the other)67 / 11030
  • Raw shares live on different scales (LLM lists around 50%, clicks around 0.1%), so the combined strength uses within-source ranks and the asymmetry uses ratios. Per-source shares are always shown next to them.
  • The news sample is light (a few thousand articles), so zeros there can mean small samples.
  • The LLM's knowledge stops in early 2025, so it misses recent deals, including Novig. Its numbers are model_predicted.
  • TikTok, YouTube and Reddit would add the sources ordinary people engage with most; they need official API access (see the earlier note).
  • Pairs were hand-picked from recent announcements, not sampled.
